To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capacity region of general Gaussian interference channels can be characterized to within a single unit of information.

1) for the complete capacity, a simplified Han-Kobyashi type scheme can attain to within a single-bit the capacity of the two-user interference channel; and 2) the capacity region of an arbitrary two-user interference channel can be characterized to within a singlebit.

(1) the existing outer bounds on the capacity region can be arbitrarily loose in the general case, (2) the Han-Kobayasi achievable region can be arbitrarily far from capacity, and (3) the capacity region can in fact be achieved to within one bit by a simplified Han-Kobyashi scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the capacity region of Gaussian interference channels.
the capacity of a two-user Gaussian interference network, where the two users can transmit information to one another as well as to a common receiver.
the capacity of Gaussian channels with multiple users and multiple transmitters and receivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capacity region is within one bit of being characterized.
the Han-Kobayshi scheme is optimal for the two-user Gaussian IC.
the capacity region of any Gaussian interference channel is within one bit of being achievable by the Han-Kobayashischeme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided an answer to the question of how much interference is needed to reduce the degrees of freedom in an interference network.
the capacity region of a Gaussian interference channel is characterized to within one bit.
we have shown that for all possible interference channels, there exists a simple scheme that achieves to within one bit the capacity region of all such channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interference does not always hurt.
the capacity of the Gaussian interference channel is not a complicated function of the channel parameters, and that the Han-Kobayshi scheme is essentially optimal.
the capacity region of a general two-user Gaussian interference is not a convex set.
